sentences.zh: 受过相似的创伤。

sentences.en: Wounded in similar ways.
sentences.zh: 受过相似的创伤。

sentences.en: It sounds like something that a hippie would say, but the truth is we're wounded in similar ways.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是嬉皮士会说的话，但事实是，我们受过相似的创伤。

sentences.en: Hey guys, it's Joel, and I'm going to try and do a quick little podcast today because I haven't done one for a minute.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是乔尔，今天我打算做一个简短的小播客，因为我已经有一段时间没做了。

sentences.en: People have requested that there be video even when it's just me talking, and they seem to rank better.
sentences.zh: 有人要求即使只有我一个人说话也要有视频，而且它们的排名似乎更好。

sentences.en: So, yeah, even though it's just me today, I will put a video up if you want to look at the bags under my eyes that badly.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，尽管今天只有我一个人，但如果你这么想看我眼袋有多重的话，我会发个视频。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 去吧。

sentences.en: So today we're going to talk about ritual and animism and some of the thinkers that I like around those things.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要聊聊仪式、万物有灵论以及我所喜欢的一些相关思想家。

sentences.en: One of the things that I think is sort of interesting, if you look at, and you can read about it in my upcoming novella in 2026,
sentences.zh: 其中一件我觉得挺有意思的事情，如果你去看看——你可以在我2026年即将出版的中篇小说里读到它——

sentences.en: but one of the things that I think is really interesting is the way that psychotic experience sort of informs,
sentences.zh: 但其中一件我觉得非常有趣的事情，就是精神病体验某种程度上如何启发了——

sentences.en: not informs, but lets us, gives us like secrets about how we think, gives us information about how we think.
sentences.zh: 不是启发，而是让我们、给我们一些关于我们如何思考的秘密，给我们提供关于我们如何思考的信息。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a huge history in psychoanalytic practice, you know, sometimes ethically, sometimes not so ethically,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在精神分析实践中有着悠久的历史，你知道，有时符合伦理，有时不太符合伦理，

sentences.en: of people seeing psychotic experiences this way where people's ego is sort of turned off,
sentences.zh: 人们以这种方式看待精神病体验，即人们的自我（ego）在某种程度上被关闭了，

sentences.en: and they're able to just tell you about these deep archetypes and functions of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 而他们能够向你讲述意识的这些深层原型和功能。

sentences.en: Like, you know, Carl Jung famously was working with people who had schizophrenia,
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，卡尔·荣格曾与患有精神分裂症的人合作而闻名，

sentences.en: and he realized that they were telling him, you know, mythology from these really elaborate systems,
sentences.zh: 他意识到他们正在向他讲述，你知道，来自这些非常复杂系统的神话，

sentences.en: some that had just been translated or the cutting edge of academia at that time.
sentences.zh: 有些刚刚被翻译出来，或者处于当时学术界的最前沿。

sentences.en: And these people were homeless and alcoholic and had no formal education, yet they're telling him Zoroastrian mythology.
sentences.zh: 而这些人无家可归、酗酒、没有受过正规教育，但他们却在向他讲述琐罗亚斯德教的神话。

sentences.en: Well, you know, how are you doing that if this is just something that somebody wrote down in the Bronze Age, and then that was a single experience?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，如果这只是某人在青铜时代写下的东西，然后那是一次孤立的经历，你是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it isn't, you know, there are perennial philosophies in how we think.
sentences.zh: 好吧，事实并非如此，你知道，我们的思维方式中存在着永恒的哲学。

sentences.en: And so not to go on too much about that, you know, this, again, is about ritual and animism and some of the ways to think about those things.
sentences.zh: 所以为了不在这上面说太多，你知道，这再次是关于仪式和万物有灵论以及思考这些事情的一些方法。

sentences.en: But I do think it is, like, relevant to go through, well, one, I guess I'll define that.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，顺便梳理一下是相关的，嗯，首先，我想我会定义一下。

sentences.en: So animism is this kind of belief that the world is alive.
sentences.zh: 所以万物有灵论是一种世界是有生命的信仰。

sentences.en: You see it in things like Japanese mythology.
sentences.zh: 你在日本神话之类的事情中能看到这一点。

sentences.en: Like, I just wrote an episode about Miyazaki, if you like his anime, you know, the guy who did Spirited Away and recently The Boy and the Heron.
sentences.zh: 就像，我刚刚写了一集关于宫崎骏的节目，如果你喜欢他的动漫，你知道，那个制作了《千与千寻》以及最近的《苍鹭与少年》的人。

sentences.en: We have an article on that on the blog.
sentences.zh: 我们在博客上有一篇关于这个的文章。

sentences.en: But this idea that there are spirits in a rock and an animal and a plant in the weather, even, you know,
sentences.zh: 但这这种观点认为，石头、动物、植物甚至天气中都有精灵，你知道，

sentences.en: and that we're sort of just in conversation with these things, that I'm alive, but also the world is alive.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在与这些事物对话，我是有生命的，但世界也是有生命的。

sentences.en: That would be an animistic worldview.
sentences.zh: 这将是一种万物有灵论的世界观。

sentences.en: You know, slightly different from pantheism, which says there's, like, tons of gods, you know, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这与泛神论略有不同，泛神论认为，到处都有无数的神明，你知道。

sentences.en: I mean, there's this, like, deep sort of natural world and all the systems that we inhabit are also alive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一种深层的自然世界，我们居住的所有系统也都是有生命的。

sentences.en: So you see in animism a lot of reverence for everything.
sentences.zh: 所以在万物有灵论中，你会看到对万物的无限敬畏。

sentences.en: Like, they tend to be cultures that don't double down on, like, greed or exploitation or, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如，他们往往是那些不会执着于贪婪、剥削或，你知道，

sentences.en: killing the natural world because you're respecting it as a living creature that you are in conversation with that has power over you.
sentences.zh: 为了消灭自然世界而将其赶尽杀绝的文化，因为你尊重它是一个有生命的生物，你正在与之对话，它对你拥有力量。

sentences.en: You know, ritual is a different thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，仪式是另一回事。

sentences.en: So ritual, I think, is, you know, when you take a set of things and it can be to enact—well, we do both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以仪式，我认为，你知道，当你采取一系列的事情，它可以是为了制定——好吧，我们同时在做这两件事。

sentences.en: We're just fighting about the causation or the reality of it, right?
sentences.zh: 我们只是在争论其因果关系或现实性，对吧？

sentences.en: Either a psychological or a metaphysical conversation that you're having through a repetitive or controlled practice, you know?
sentences.zh: 通过重复或受控的实践，你正在进行的心理或形而上学的对话，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So if you go to church and you have communion, like, that's a ritual because what you're doing is you're saying,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你去教堂领圣餐，这算是一个仪式，因为你所做的是你在说，

sentences.en: I remember Jesus had a Last Supper, and I remember that the Last Supper was a metaphor for him going to die for me,
sentences.zh: 我记得耶稣吃过最后晚餐，我记得最后晚餐是他为我而死的隐喻，

sentences.en: and, you know, his body is bread, his blood is wine, and he said this when he did this,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他的身体是面包，他的血是酒，他在做这件事时是这么说的，

sentences.en: and now we continue to do this in remembrance of him, you know, in the Episcopal Church, that's what they say.
sentences.zh: 现在我们继续这样做来纪念他，你知道，在圣公会教堂里，他们就是这么说的。

sentences.en: So, you know, that is a ritual where we are saying that this thing is connecting us to either psychological or a metaphysical reality or a little bit of both.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那是一个仪式，我们在其中说这件事正在将我们连接到心理或形而上学的现实，或者两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: And animism, one way to think about it is that you're taking your psychology, your consciousness, and you're turning it down.
sentences.zh: 而万物有灵论，思考它的一个方法是，你把你的心理、你的意识调低了。

sentences.en: You know, your ability to be like—the responsibility is turned down a little bit of like, I have to understand the entire world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你作为——这种责任被稍微调低了一点，比如我必须理解整个世界。

sentences.en: I have to know everything.
sentences.zh: 我必须了解一切。

sentences.en: I am the only thing that is alive, and I'm taking this image of this other person and this image of this other person and this image of the mountain,
sentences.zh: 我是唯一活着的东西，我把这个人的这个形象、那个人的那个形象以及山的那个形象拿来，

sentences.en: and I have to know how to build the engine, and I have to—you're turning that down a little bit,
sentences.zh: 我必须知道如何制造发动机，我必须——你把这个稍微调低了一点，

sentences.en: and you're becoming sort of like less conscious or less solely responsible for the conscious ordering of the world so that you can hear the rest of the world be alive.
sentences.zh: 你变得有点像不那么有意识，或者不再独自承担世界有意识排序的责任，这样你就能听到世界上其余部分是有生命的。

sentences.en: You know, and you can—somebody may be listening to this, and they may be pagan or lean animistic and believe in these things as a literal force.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以——有人可能会听这个，他们可能是异教徒，或者倾向于万物有灵论，并将这些事情视为一种字面上的力量。

sentences.en: You know, other people are going to understand that as a psychological or anthropological reality, but that's a way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其他人会将其理解为一种心理或人类学现实，但这是思考它的一种方式。

sentences.en: I'm turning my consciousness down a little bit, my inner voice down a little bit, so that I can hear the world speak or I can hear the world be alive.
sentences.zh: 我把我的意识稍微调低了一点，把我内心的声音稍微调低了一点，这样我就可以听到世界说话，或者我就可以听到世界充满生机。

sentences.en: Ritual, I think, is when you take these forces of the unconscious, these emotional realities in the brainstem,
sentences.zh: 仪式，我认为，当你把无意识的这些力量、脑干中的这些情感现实，

sentences.en: and you project them onto objects to do a reenactment of something or to have power over something in this external way to later have it reflect this internal reality.
sentences.zh: 将它们投射到物体上以重现某事，或者以这种外部方式对某事拥有权力，以便稍后让它反映这种内部现实。

sentences.en: So, say I want to go do a spell.
sentences.zh: 所以，假设我想去施个法。

sentences.en: Like, I want to go down to the pagan store, and I'm going to do a spell with some candles.
sentences.zh: 比如，我想去异教徒商店，我要用一些蜡烛施个法。

sentences.en: And I look at, you know, astrology that speaks to the significance of how I do the ritual, and I say, I broke up with my girlfriend, boyfriend, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我看看，你知道，符合我如何进行仪式的意义的占星术，我说，我和女朋友、男朋友或随便什么人分手了。

sentences.en: I'm very sad about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到很难过。

sentences.en: I don't want to be sad anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不想再难过了。

sentences.en: And why am I sad?
sentences.zh: 我为什么难过？

sentences.en: I'm sad because I'm missing this thing that is a part of me.
sentences.zh: 我难过是因为我想念这个属于我一部分的东西。

sentences.en: And so I take a candle, and I light it on fire, and I do a ritual where I say, this is me, you know, this little candle, and it's missing this piece,
sentences.zh: 所以我拿了一支蜡烛，把它点燃，我做一个仪式，我说，这是我，你知道，这支小蜡烛，它缺少了这一部分，

sentences.en: so I'm going to let it burn all the way down.
sentences.zh: 所以我要让它一直燃烧到底。

sentences.en: And now that it's burning all the way down and going out, I'm going to get another candle.
sentences.zh: 现在它一直燃烧到底并熄灭了，我要拿另一支蜡烛。

sentences.en: So this represents, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这代表，你知道，

sentences.en: this depleted and reduced and depressed and sad me that has been burned all the way down to the ground over the time that I've done my drum circle ritual represents the old me.
sentences.zh: 这个疲惫、减少、沮丧、悲伤的我，在我进行鼓圈仪式的这段时间里被烧成了灰烬，代表着过去的那个我。

sentences.en: And I'm going to light this new candle, which represents the new me in all of its fullness that is now not missing anything that has been restored.
sentences.zh: 我要点亮这支新蜡烛，它代表着崭新的我，充满活力，现在不再缺少任何东西，已经恢复完整。

sentences.en: And I'm going to take, you know, in the ritual circle, this old candle away, or turn the disc that it's on so that it's in a different position, and then put the new candle there.
sentences.zh: 我要把，你知道，在仪式圈里，把这支旧蜡烛拿走，或者转动它所在的盘子，让它处于不同的位置，然后把新蜡烛放在那里。

sentences.en: And what I've done is I've said, I'm no longer sad, I am okay, I'm enough, I'm whole, after this setback internally.
sentences.zh: 而我所做的是我说，我不再难过了，我很好，我足够了，我是完整的，在经历这次内部挫折之后。

sentences.en: I've said that externally, right?
sentences.zh: 我在外部表达了这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: So that I can later say the internal reality that this thing that I was doing was describing has changed.
sentences.zh: 这样我以后就可以说，我正在做的事情所描述的内在现实已经改变了。

sentences.en: Now that I can withdraw this projection back inside of me, and I can feel like I've changed this internal reality of being sad through this external practice.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以把这个投射收回我体内，我觉得我通过这种外部实践改变了这种悲伤的内在现实。

sentences.en: Or this external, maybe it's an external thing that you want, like a new job or something, you're doing a ritual to get it.
sentences.zh: 或者这种外部的东西，也许它是你想要的外部事物，比如一份新工作什么的，你正在通过仪式来获得它。

sentences.en: But that's one way of thinking about ritual, is that you're projecting on these objects, then internal reality, moving them around,
sentences.zh: 但这是思考仪式的一种方式，即你将内部现实投射到这些物体上，四处移动它们，

sentences.en: and then withdrawing the projection to have back, you know, that change.
sentences.zh: 然后收回投射，你知道，从而获得那种改变。

sentences.en: Change.
sentences.zh: 改变。

sentences.en: You're wanting change.
sentences.zh: 你想要改变。

sentences.en: You want some results from it.
sentences.zh: 你希望从中得到一些结果。

sentences.en: Whereas animism is a sort of giving up control.
sentences.zh: 而万物有灵论是一种放弃控制。

sentences.en: You know, ritual is a taking control.
sentences.zh: 你知道，仪式是一种掌控。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of different kinds of ritual.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多不同种类的仪式。

sentences.en: I mean, this can't go through the entire history of how these things work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不可能穷尽这些事情运作的整个历史。

sentences.en: But the relationship to something like animism and ritual to psychotic experience is interesting, because like, you can be psychotic and go to church and take communion.
sentences.zh: 但万物有灵论和仪式之类的东西与精神病体验的关系很有趣，因为就像，你可能会精神错乱去教堂领圣餐。

sentences.en: But most people who go to church and do communion are not psychotic.
sentences.zh: 但大多数去教堂领圣餐的人并没有精神错乱。

sentences.en: You could, I guess, be psychotic, you know, when you're, when you are psychotic, you may have animistic phenomenon where you hear, you know, things, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想你可能是精神错乱的，你知道，当你精神错乱时，你可能会有万物有灵论的现象，你会听到，你知道，一些东西，你知道，

sentences.en: that otherwise are not there speaking to you.
sentences.zh: 平时不在那里的东西在跟你说话。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean I don't think everybody who believes in animism, who experiences it is psychotic, because for a large period of our development, I mean,
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我不认为每个相信万物有灵论、经历过它的人都是精神错乱的，因为在我们发展的很长一段时期里，我的意思是，

sentences.en: this episode is kind of a sequel to that Neolithic anthropology, that architecture, Neolithic architecture, one about the dolmen, because a lot of people responded.
sentences.zh: 这一集有点像是对新石器时代人类学、建筑学、新石器时代建筑学那期（关于支前石墓的那期）的续集，因为很多人都作出了回应。

sentences.en: And this is a follow up to that.
sentences.zh: 这是对此的后续。

sentences.en: But remember, for a large part of our existence, like our humanity, like we were sort of animistic, or if you want to call that psychotic,
sentences.zh: 但请记住，在我们存在的很大一部分时间里，就像我们的人性一样，我们有点像万物有灵论者，或者如果你想把那叫做精神错乱，

sentences.en: then you're saying that humans were psychotic up to fairly recently on the timeline.
sentences.zh: 那么你就是在说人类在时间线上的相当晚近之前都是精神错乱的。

sentences.en: I mean, more recently than the brain changed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比大脑发生变化的时间还要晚近。

sentences.en: So then I think there were, if you want to define psychosis as any participation in religion like this, which I don't think most people do, I've heard some people say that,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，如果你想把精神病定义为任何对这种宗教的参与，虽然我认为大多数人不会这么认为，但我听过有些人这么说，

sentences.en: then you have to kind of see that the forces of consciousness as more of a cultural phenomenon than an evolutionary one.
sentences.zh: 那么你必须把意识的力量视为一种文化现象，而不是进化现象。

sentences.en: Because we were living this way up until fairly recently, where there were just sort of assumptions about how things worked, that were part of our life that we heard.
sentences.zh: 因为直到不久前我们一直以这种方式生活，当时关于事情如何运作只是有一些假设，那是我们生活的一部分，我们听到了这些声音。

sentences.en: And one of the early people who kind of examines this is James Frazier, if you've ever read The Golden Bough.
sentences.zh: 而最早研究这一点的人之一是詹姆斯·弗雷泽，如果你读过《金枝》的话。

sentences.en: And James Frazier is like a really early anthropologist,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·弗雷泽就像一个非常早期的人类学家，

sentences.en: who is going through these different ways of thinking and trying to figure out what it is that makes mythology of the ancient world and the modernist conception of gods and everything.
sentences.zh: 他正在梳理这些不同的思维方式，并试图弄清楚到底是什么构成了古代世界的神话以及现代主义对神明及一切事物的概念。

sentences.en: What changed?
sentences.zh: 什么变了？

sentences.en: You know, why do people think so differently now than they did?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么现在人们的想法与过去如此不同？

sentences.en: I would argue that they don't really.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们实际上并没有变。

sentences.en: So, you know, James Frazier writes The Golden Bough in, I think, like 1890.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，詹姆斯·弗雷泽在大约1890年写了《金枝》。

sentences.en: And it gets, it's controversial, it gets kind of more popular until the 20s.
sentences.zh: 它引发了争议，并且越来越受欢迎，直到20年代。

sentences.en: But it's this comparative study of mythology and religion that looks at these different patterns in religion and the way that people believe things.
sentences.zh: 但这是一项对神话和宗教的比较研究，着眼于宗教中的这些不同模式以及人们信仰事物的方式。

sentences.en: He's influenced by Tyner's work on animism.
sentences.zh: 他受到泰勒关于万物有灵论工作的启发。

sentences.en: And one of the things that Frazier is looking at is how ritual is this means of controlling the supernatural, that you're controlling something and then you're,
sentences.zh: 弗雷泽正在研究的事情之一是仪式如何成为控制超自然的一种手段，你正在控制某种东西，然后你——

sentences.en: and so he comes up with this idea of sympathetic magic that like produces like.
sentences.zh: 因此他提出了同类巫术的概念，即同类产生同类。

sentences.en: Like if you do a tiny ritual play of rain with dolls or corn or something, that that will actually, because that is like, you know, greater reality of this universe,
sentences.zh: 就像如果你用玩偶、玉米或其他东西做一个小型的降雨仪式游戏，这实际上会——因为这类似于，你知道，这个宇宙更伟大的现实，

sentences.en: that the universe will hear it and respond to it.
sentences.zh: 宇宙会听到它并做出回应。

sentences.en: And there's a synthesis between your recreation of this thing in a microcosm and the macrocosm reality that you're trying to control, either to get something out of the universe,
sentences.zh: 在你对微观世界中这件事的再创造与你试图控制的宏观世界现实之间存在着一种综合，无论是为了从宇宙中获得某种东西，

sentences.en: like the physical natural world or in the emotional sphere inside of you or both.
sentences.zh: 比如物理自然世界，还是在你内部的情感领域，或者两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: You know, there's rituals, I think, where you're taking, you know, the little thing and you're modeling a supernatural reality.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为有些仪式，你拿着小东西来模拟超自然现实。

sentences.en: And there's ones where you're modeling an internal reality of I want to get over a breakup or I want it to rain on my crops.
sentences.zh: 还有一些仪式，你是在模拟一种内在现实，即我想从失恋中走出来，或者我希望我的庄稼下雨。

sentences.en: Those are two different rituals.
sentences.zh: 这是两种不同的仪式。

sentences.en: And then there are places, you know, probably like something like communion or most of the major religions, the things that endure become more broad, where you're doing both.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些地方，你知道，可能类似于圣餐或大多数主要宗教，那些经久不衰的事物变得更加广泛，在这些地方你两者兼顾。

sentences.en: You're talking about a psychological inner state in you or a spiritual inner state in you and a bigger state in the world.
sentences.zh: 你在谈论你内部的心理状态或精神状态，以及世界上更大的状态。

sentences.en: You know, there's rituals that do one, the other, both.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些仪式只做一种，或者另一种，或者两者兼顾。

sentences.en: And somebody who comes after Frasier, Julian Jaynes,
sentences.zh: 弗雷泽之后的另一个人是朱利安·杰恩斯，

sentences.en: Jaynes is one of those people who I think he's looking at something that is like an unavoidable reality that you have to look at, but that also you're going to.
sentences.zh: 杰恩斯是那种我认为他在关注某种不可避免的现实的人，你必须去面对它，但你也将——

sentences.en: Be describing that unavoidable perennial reality with a metaphor and Jaynes's metaphor is probably not the most popular.
sentences.zh: 用隐喻来描述那种不可避免的永恒现实，而杰恩斯的隐喻可能不是最受欢迎的。

sentences.en: It doesn't really work.
sentences.zh: 它其实并不奏效。

sentences.en: So in 76, he publishes the origin of consciousness and the breakdown of the bicameral mind, which is about bicameralism.
sentences.zh: 所以在76年，他出版了《意识的起源与二分心智的崩溃》，这是关于二分心智论的。

sentences.en: And there's this idea that the reason that in Greek mythology, you know, we heard gods and people just said, oh, the altar speaking to me or whatever.
sentences.zh: 有这样一个观点，为什么在希腊神话中，你知道，我们听到神明说话，人们只会说，哦，是圣坛在跟我说话之类的。

sentences.en: Um, the reason that that existed is because, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，之所以存在这种情况，是因为，呃，

sentences.en: we just had a mind that was evolutionary and biologically different where the creative side of my mind was not cut off from the logical yet, um, biologically.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚拥有了一个进化和生物学上不同的心智，其中我心智的创造性一面在生物学上尚未与逻辑切断。

sentences.en: And so it would just tell me information and I would hear Poseidon talk to me when I was trying to get home to Ithaca and I would just hear Athena, um, tell me, uh,
sentences.zh: 所以它会直接告诉我信息，当我试图回到伊萨卡时，我会听到波塞冬跟我说话，而在帕台农神庙或德尔斐神谕所献祭之后，我就会听到雅典娜，呃，

sentences.en: that I was going to win this war after I made an offering, you know, at the Parthenon or the Oracle of Delphi, maybe, you know, it wasn't so much the gas she was huffing.
sentences.zh: 告诉我，我将赢得这场战争，你知道，可能不是因为她吸了毒气。

sentences.en: She was just hearing the voice of the God more.
sentences.zh: 她只是更多地听到了神的声音。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: and he's saying that biologically we used to hear our ideas as physical realities and that slowly the unconscious mind kind of separated and became something that we could ignore more,
sentences.zh: 他说，从生物学上讲，我们曾经把自己的想法当作物理现实来听取，渐渐地，无意识的心智某种程度上分离开来，变成了一种我们可以更多地忽视的东西，

sentences.en: but it was still there.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然在那里。

sentences.en: Um, but we no longer heard it directly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我们不再直接听到它了。

sentences.en: And I mean, I, the book is interesting depending on how literally you want to read it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这本书很有趣，取决于你想按字面意思读到什么程度。

sentences.en: Um, James dies feeling like he's not wrong, but he didn't really say what he wanted to say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，詹姆斯去世时觉得自己没有错，但他并没有真正说出他想说的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Um, his perspective is definitely this reaction to behaviorism, like all the behaviorists.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他的观点绝对是对行为主义的一种反应，就像所有的行为主义者一样。

sentences.en: Uh, I think the line that he says is that, um, they solve the problem of consciousness by ignoring it, that you can say that you've solved, uh,
sentences.zh: 呃，我想他说的一句话是，呃，他们通过忽视意识来解决意识问题，你可以说你已经解决了，呃，

sentences.en: how cognition and the inner monologue works.
sentences.zh: 认知和内心独白是如何运作的。

sentences.en: If you only study behavior, introduce everything down to empiricism, um, which is, it's funny, um, because that is the study of behavior and the study of, I think,
sentences.zh: 如果你只研究行为，把一切都归结为经验主义，呃，这是，这很有趣，呃，

sentences.en: cognition are related, but separate.
sentences.zh: 因为行为研究和认知研究是相关的，但又是独立的。

sentences.en: And, um, but don't tell that to a behaviorist or a cognitive behavioral therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，但千万别对行为主义者或认知行为治疗师这么说。

sentences.en: So, um, what James is doing is trying to explain why animism and ritual went away, or we have a different relationship to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，詹姆斯正在做的是试图解释为什么万物有灵论和仪式消失了，或者我们与它们有了不同的关系。

sentences.en: And he's trying to ground that in an evolutionary change in the brain.
sentences.zh: 他正试图将这一点建立在大脑的进化变化基础之上。

sentences.en: But the problem is it isn't an evolutionary change in the brain.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，这不是大脑的进化变化。

sentences.en: It's not a biological change.
sentences.zh: 这不是生物学上的改变。

sentences.en: It is a cultural change, you know, um, because these animistic states, these ritual states, they're muscle, they're much less common, but they are still possible.
sentences.zh: 这是一种文化上的改变，你知道，嗯，因为这些万物有灵论状态、这些仪式状态，它们已经不那么常见了，但它们仍然是可能的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: You know, like a ton of people, um, have emailed me about how they want me to go to this ayahuasca cult that they do, or not cult in a bad way, but there's like a group,
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像超级多的人，嗯，给我发邮件说他们想让我去参加他们搞的那种死藤水邪教，或者说不是那种坏意义上的邪教，而是一个群体，

sentences.en: it's not just one of them.
sentences.zh: 不止一个这样的群体。

sentences.en: Multiple people have said like, Oh, I like your podcasts, whatever.
sentences.zh: 好几个人都说，哦，我喜欢你的播客之类的。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: I'm not, I'm not going to go do ayahuasca, but I would imagine that if I did, um, you know, fly to the Amazon or whatever, uh,
sentences.zh: 我不会去喝死藤水，但我可以想象，如果我真的去了，比如说，飞到亚马逊或者什么地方，呃，

sentences.en: that I could have a very animistic experience on this drug.
sentences.zh: 我在这类药物的作用下，可能会有一种非常具有万物有灵论色彩的体验。

sentences.en: Maybe if I inhabited that world, talk to those shamans, embodied their reality for a really long time, learn to like turn part of my brain off and listen to the trees,
sentences.zh: 也许如果我融入那个世界，和那些萨满交谈，长时间地去体悟他们的现实，学会关掉大脑的一部分去倾听树木，

sentences.en: I would just start knowing, you know, on this kind of intuitive, spiritual way that it was about to start to rain based on changes in the way the world smelled,
sentences.zh: 我就会开始明白，通过这种直觉的、精神的方式，比如根据世界上气味的变化，

sentences.en: based on changes in the way that the world looked, you know, patterns of light, um, wind patterns, you know, my unconscious,
sentences.zh: 根据世界上视觉景观的变化，你知道的，光影模式、风向模式，还有我的无意识，

sentences.en: if I inhabited that space would just start to intuitively notice these things.
sentences.zh: 如果我融入那个空间，就会开始凭直觉注意到这些事情。

sentences.en: You know, if I could really turn intuition on and when you really turn it on a lot, there is, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我真的能开启直觉，而当你真正大量开启它时，就会有，

sentences.en: this unfiltered information where some of those things feel like a message or a knowing or a voice, which a lot of people are scared of because that's also what psychosis is,
sentences.zh: 这种未经过滤的信息，其中有些东西感觉像是一个信息、一种领悟或是一个声音，很多人对此感到害怕，因为这也是精神病发作时的表现，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like psychosis is just knowing something without there being any evidence or ability to reality teSt.
sentences.zh: 就像精神病发作只是在没有任何证据或现实检验能力的情况下知道某些事情一样。

sentences.en: You know, your creative mind just comes up with something,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的创造性思维只是想出了一些东西，

sentences.en: but your ability to discern what's creativity created for me and what's an outer reality picked up on my senses is just gone.
sentences.zh: 但你分辨什么是自己创造的创意、什么是感官捕捉到的外部现实的能力却完全消失了。

sentences.en: You know, I had a patient, um, long, long, long time ago when I first started social work as an intern who, um,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很久很久以前，在我刚开始做社工实习生的时候，有一个病人，呃，

sentences.en: was very well-spoken and he also was unmedicated and had schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 他很会说话，而且没有吃药，患有精神分裂症。

sentences.en: And I asked him one time, I said, you know,
sentences.zh: 有一次我问他，我说，你知道，

sentences.en: you're always telling me you figured out what the government's doing with the lasers and that the satellite's here and it's going to beam these words into your head and, and,
sentences.zh: 你总是告诉我，你弄明白了政府在用激光做什么，卫星就在这里，它要把这些话打入你的脑子里，而且，而且，

sentences.en: and different things.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: And you used to read a lot, you go to the library and there were books about gang stalking or books, other people write about these things.
sentences.zh: 你以前读很多书，你去图书馆，那里有关于跟踪狂的书，或者其他人写这些事情的书。

sentences.en: And you would learn from that.
sentences.zh: 你会从中吸取知识。

sentences.en: And then you stopped doing that when your car quit working.
sentences.zh: 然后当你的车坏了之后，你就停止了这样做。

sentences.en: And then you used to have internet.
sentences.zh: 然后你以前有网络。

sentences.en: So you get on your phone and you'd get on these forums and people talk about how they were persecuted and you would figure things out that way.
sentences.zh: 所以你用手机登录这些论坛，人们谈论他们是如何受到迫害的，你就是这样弄懂这些事情的。

sentences.en: But you've just kind of been in your house alone for a year.
sentences.zh: 但你一个人在家里待了一年。

sentences.en: You haven't gotten on the internet cause you hadn't had it.
sentences.zh: 你没有上网，因为你没有网。

sentences.en: You hadn't gone out to get these things.
sentences.zh: 你也没有出门去弄这些东西。

sentences.en: So how do you, how are you figuring this out?
sentences.zh: 所以你是怎么，你是怎么搞懂这些的？

sentences.en: You know, just alone in your house, you're talking about satellites in space.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就独自呆在家里，你却在谈论太空中的卫星。

sentences.en: And he told me something that is the best description of a delusion.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我的一句话，是对妄想症最好的描述。

sentences.en: I think phenomenologically you're ever going to get, which was you get that feeling where you're wondering if something is true and you start wondering if it's true or not,
sentences.zh: 我认为从现象学上来说，你永远也得不到比这更好的描述了，那就是：你会有那种感觉，你想知道某事是否属实，你开始怀疑它是否属实，

sentences.en: but then you just know that it is.
sentences.zh: 但随后你就是知道它是真的。

sentences.en: And you don't have to do that thing where you figure it out.
sentences.zh: 而且你不需要去做那种去把事情弄清楚的过程。

sentences.en: So when you, when people hear animism, ritual, whatever, you know, religious experience,
sentences.zh: 所以当人们听到万物有灵论、仪式，或者别的什么，你知道的，宗教体验，

sentences.en: I think a lot of times they think you have to be stupid or you have to be delusional to participate in these things, which it isn't.
sentences.zh: 我想很多时候他们会认为你必须很愚蠢或者有妄想症才会参与这些事情，其实并不是这样的。

sentences.en: I mean, whether or not, and I'm not even really saying if it's a good thing or a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无论如何——甚至我都不是在说这是一件好事还是一件坏事。

sentences.en: I mean, I think respecting the planet a little bit more, um, treating it like a living system that we are in communication with, um, might prolong our species a little bit longer.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为多尊重一点这个星球，呃，把它当作一个我们与之进行沟通的生命系统，呃，可能会让我们的物种多延续一会儿。

sentences.en: But I'm not even saying, you know, what your religious experience should be or what our relationship should be.
sentences.zh: 但我甚至不是在说，你知道，你的宗教体验应该是什么样的，或者我们之间的关系应该是什么样的。

sentences.en: I'm just saying that the evolutionary capacity for these states of mind is still present in the species.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，这些精神状态的进化能力在这个物种中依然存在。

sentences.en: Like we are still, we want to say, okay, we're modern and they used to be ancient, but that change is cultural.
sentences.zh: 就像我们仍然——我们总想说，好吧，我们是现代的，而他们过去是古代的，但这种变化是文化的。

sentences.en: It's not environmental.
sentences.zh: 它不是环境的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's environmental.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它是，它是环境的。

sentences.en: It's not biological.
sentences.zh: 它不是生物学的。

sentences.en: Um, you know, the modern human and the ancient human are, are the same.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道，现代人和古代人是，是一样的。

sentences.en: And so we have the capacity for these states.
sentences.zh: 因此我们具备进入这些状态的能力。

sentences.en: And I think when you think about them, they explain a lot of our culture and a lot of the way that parts of our world work.
sentences.zh: 我想当你思考它们时，它们解释了我们的很多文化以及我们世界某些部分的运作方式。

sentences.en: Um, there's a huge meta analysis that I used when I wrote the spider in the birdhouse, which is like, um, uh, a novella that I had published.
sentences.zh: 呃，我写《蜘蛛在鸟屋里》时用过一个大型的元分析，那是一本，呃，我出版的中篇小说。

sentences.en: It's supposed to come out this summer, but it's actually coming out next summer.
sentences.zh: 它本该在今年夏天出版，但实际上会在明年夏天出版。

sentences.en: Now, um, the publisher wanted to, to wait.
sentences.zh: 现在，呃，出版商想要，想要等一等。

sentences.en: Um, so when I was writing that there's this huge meta analysis of like all of these studies, um, on psychosis that the government had commissioned, uh, going back forever.
sentences.zh: 呃，所以当我写那本书的时候，有这样一个关于精神病研究的大型元分析，呃，这些研究是政府委托的，可以追溯到很久很久以前。

sentences.en: It was paid for it for some, um, probably NIS or something.
sentences.zh: 它是由某个，呃，可能是国家心理健康研究所（NIMH）或类似的机构资助的。

sentences.en: I don't remember.
sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.en: I don't have the citation anymore.
sentences.zh: 我手头已经没有引用文献了。

sentences.en: I did this when I was in grad school, but there's this giant study on like the evolution of psychosis in America.
sentences.zh: 我在读研究生时做过这个，但有一个关于美国精神病演变的巨型研究。

sentences.en: Um, and how you read that as a behaviorist and you don't change what you think, I don't understand.
sentences.zh: 呃，作为一个行为主义者，你怎么能那样解读它却不改变你的想法，我实在无法理解。

sentences.en: Um, but one of the things was that, you know, essentially like pre, um, like pre depression era psychotic states looks a lot like animism.
sentences.zh: 呃，但其中有一点是，你知道的，基本上在萧条期之前，呃，比如大萧条前的精神病状态看起来非常像万物有灵论。

sentences.en: People just spoke to things that either had ancestral or geographic features.
sentences.zh: 人们只是对那些具有祖先或地理特征的事物说话。

sentences.en: So you'd have people that were just saying like, they're talking to the spirit of their mother or their great grandmother, you know, something just pops up.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到有人只是在说，他们在和母亲或曾祖母的灵魂对话，你知道，有些东西就这样突然冒出来了。

sentences.en: And then most of the, with schizophrenia, especially most of what you're going to get, unless there's any kind of substance use, it's just going to be an auditory hallucination.
sentences.zh: 然后大多数精神分裂症患者，尤其是大多数你会遇到的情况，除非有任何形式的物质滥用，否则基本都只是听觉幻觉。

sentences.en: You're not really going to see things.
sentences.zh: 你并不是真的看到了什么东西。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's what they would hear.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这就是他们会听到的声音。

sentences.en: If somebody was schizophrenic or somebody went into a psychotic state due to trauma, also geographic, you know, the thing that lived in the river, the town, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果有人患有精神分裂症，或者有人因创伤而进入精神病状态，同样也是地理性的，你知道的，住在河里、镇上的那个东西，你知道的，

sentences.en: it was the nature of these things kind of spoke to you and, and largely they weren't distressing.
sentences.zh: 这些东西的本质似乎在对你说话，而且在很大程度上它们并不会令人感到痛苦。

sentences.en: I mean, sometimes people aren't as productive when they're psychotic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有时候人们精神失常时效率没那么高。

sentences.en: Um, but the, the town and the people kind of compensated for it.
sentences.zh: 呃，但是小镇和人们在某种程度上弥补了这一点。

sentences.en: The, the idea of the people who were spiritual or people who go into psychosis become violent just wasn't a bias that Americans had.
sentences.zh: 富有灵性的人或陷入精神病状态的人会变得暴力的这种想法，并不是美国人所具有的偏见。

sentences.en: Cause it wasn't a reality that we had.
sentences.zh: 因为那不是我们所拥有的现实。

sentences.en: And then during the depression, what would happen largely is those voices started to change into, um, asking for, uh, help.
sentences.zh: 然后在经济大萧条时期，通常发生的情况是，那些声音开始变成，呃，呼求，呃，帮助。

sentences.en: It was like, they were needy, they were hurting, they were hungry, they were tired.
sentences.zh: 就好像，他们需要帮助，他们很痛苦，他们饿了，他们累了。

sentences.en: They'd ask if you could help them or they would just be crying.
sentences.zh: 他们会问你能不能帮帮他们，或者他们只是在哭泣。

sentences.en: But there was still this through line of like empathy, um, and compassion in them.
sentences.zh: 但其中仍然有一种关于同理心和同情心的精神贯穿始终，呃，

sentences.en: Like they were, uh, uh, grateful, um, if people spoke to them or help them.
sentences.zh: 就像如果有人对他们说话或帮助他们，他们会，呃，心存感激，呃。

sentences.en: And then also a lot of times they were encouraging you to help others.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，它们还在鼓励你去帮助别人。

sentences.en: So it wasn't even asking for something.
sentences.zh: 所以甚至不是在索取什么。

sentences.zh: 关乎如何处理信息，以至于在中间必须某种组织原则。

sentences.en: And when that happened, we were, that organizing principle of consciousness, this introverted, or it created to say, no, no, no, I'm going to pick between these drives.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，我们，意识的那种组织原则——这种内倾的倾向，或者它创造出来宣告：不，不，不，我要在这些驱力之间做出选择。

sentences.en: I'm going to be something separate from them so that I can still hear the evolutionary language,
sentences.zh: 我要成为一个独立于它们的存在，这样我仍然能听到进化的语言，

sentences.en: but I can decide when I want to apply it and which one to apply when these evolutionary forces are disagreeing with one another.
sentences.zh: 但当这些进化的力量彼此发生分歧时，我可以决定何时以及应用哪一个。

sentences.en: I mean, if you want to look at neurobiology, I think that's extremely related to the development of the precuneus, because the precuneus in the brain gave us this sense of self.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想看看神经生物学，我认为这与楔前叶的发育密切相关，因为大脑中的楔前叶赋予了我们这种自我感。

sentences.en: You'll see, like, on a QEG, precuneal dysregulation in most trauma patients that have an impaired sense of ability to integrate self and world,
sentences.zh: 你会发现，比如在定量脑电图上，大多数创伤患者都会出现楔前叶失调，他们整合自我与世界的能力受损，

sentences.en: because this part of the brain is essentially, like, the hub where multiple other parts of the brain that have different agreements about how to handle information
sentences.zh: 因为这部分大脑本质上就像是一个枢纽，大脑中处理信息的多个不同部分在此交汇，

sentences.en: are crossing paths and being reconciled.
sentences.zh: 彼此交叉并达成调和。

sentences.en: So, like, of course, it's going to be a little stressed if that's a task that is impossible.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这是一项不可能完成的任务，它当然会感到有点压力。

sentences.en: So, what Neumann is saying is that these things, these drives, needed to be forgotten by the mind in order for it to manage them.
sentences.zh: 因此，诺伊曼所说的是，心灵为了管理这些东西、这些驱力，必须将它们遗忘。

sentences.en: But now that creates another problem,
sentences.zh: 但现在这又带来了另一个问题，

sentences.en: because when the ego is weak or the self is traumatized or the ego is turned off because you took LSD or you have schizophrenia or you have enough trauma to create a psychotic experience or maybe you dissociate when you go into lots of things.
sentences.zh: 因为当自我虚弱、自我受到创伤，或者因为你服用了LSD、患有精神分裂症而关闭了自我，或者你经历了足够多的创伤引发了精神病发作，又或者你在陷入诸多事务时发生解离。

sentences.en: Those forces become unmanaged and then they start to be unconscious emotional reactions that can't be understood logically.
sentences.zh: 这些力量就会失控，然后开始变成无法通过逻辑理解的无意识情绪反应。

sentences.en: And so, the ego is going to be very inclined to deny them and say, oh, those just aren't real.
sentences.zh: 因此，自我会非常倾向于否认它们，并说，哦，那些根本不真实。

sentences.en: They're not there.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不存在。

sentences.en: I didn't really say that or I said that because, which is what somebody with schizophrenia is doing.
sentences.zh: 我其实没说过那样的话，或者我说是因为……这正是精神分裂症患者会做的事。

sentences.en: But it's also the way that everyone deflects when I'm like, no, every single time in marriage counseling, your wife says this, you get upset.
sentences.zh: 但这也是每个人在面对时进行辩解的方式，当我说：不，在婚姻咨询里，每一次你妻子这么说，你都会生气。

sentences.en: Oh, no, I was just in a bad mood.
sentences.zh: 噢，没有啦，我只是当时心情不好。

sentences.en: I just ate a thing.
sentences.zh: 我只是刚好吃了点东西。

sentences.en: Okay, well, 80 times in a row, well, I just, okay, that's the way that all of us don't want to pretend that our emotional reality, you know,
sentences.zh: 好吧，连续80次都这样，好吧，这就是我们所有人都不愿意假装我们的情感现实，你知道的，

sentences.en: that archetypal subjective experience that's down there still has power over us.
sentences.zh: 那种深层的、原型的主观体验仍然对我们有着控制力。

sentences.en: And if we don't notice that, we can't integrate it and it can't be something that the ego notices and uses.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不注意到这一点，我们就无法整合它，它也无法成为自我能够注意到并加以利用的东西。

sentences.en: So, an annoyment is interesting, origins and history of consciousness.
sentences.zh: 所以，诺伊曼很有趣，写了《意识的起源与历史》。

sentences.zh: 我也非常喜欢爱德华·埃丁格。

sentences.zh: 但爱德华·埃丁格在他的书《自我与原型》中谈到，你知道，存在着自我与本我（自我与原型）。

sentences.en: And I think that he doesn't mention Frasier, at least if he does.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他没有提到弗雷泽，至少如果没有的话。

sentences.en: So, I don't think he does.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得他没有。

sentences.en: Someone's going to send me an email, but I don't remember.

sentences.zh: 如果它在那儿，它就在那儿；如果不在，就不在。

sentences.zh: 爱德华·埃丁格绝对知道他是谁。

sentences.en: I don't remember him mentioning Frasier, but so much of his work is going back and sort of like rewriting a better version of what Frasier and James are doing.
sentences.zh: 我不记得他提到了弗雷泽，但他的很多工作都在回溯并试图重写一个更好的版本，来阐述弗雷泽和詹姆斯所做的事情。

sentences.en: And like Ego and Archetype is essentially saying that we used to be, you know, unconscious animals that were part of nature.
sentences.zh: 就像《自我与原型》基本上是在说，我们曾经是，你知道的，作为自然一部分的无意识动物。

sentences.en: We slowly developed this logical consciousness and we kind of want to go back into this animistic state.
sentences.zh: 我们慢慢发展出这种逻辑意识，而我们某种程度上又想回到这种万物有灵的状态。

sentences.en: But we realize that if we do, we aren't really alive in a way that we understand or we aren't really conscious in a way that we associate with our identity.
sentences.zh: 但我们意识到，如果我们这样做了，我们就不是以我们所理解的那种方式真正活着，也不是以我们与自我认同相关联的那种方式真正具有意识。

sentences.en: So, it's this confusing experience, that kind of push and pull.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种令人困惑的体验，那种推与拉的力量。

sentences.en: But also that we have this objective reality of what I can see, taste, touch, count, you know, ego, consciousness, objective with a subjective reality of what I feel,
sentences.zh: 但同时我们也拥有客观现实，即我能看到、尝到、触摸到、数出来的东西，你知道，自我，意识，客观性，以及主观现实，即我的感受，

sentences.en: a mystical nature of self.
sentences.zh: 一种自我的神秘本质。

sentences.en: You know, maybe I can't see it, but I feel connected to the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许我看不见它，但我感觉自己与世界相连。

sentences.en: I feel interdependent on it.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己与它相互依存。

sentences.en: You know, from an emotional relational standpoint,
sentences.zh: 你知道，从情感关系的角度来看，

sentences.en: it is true that the world is a giant living breathing organism that is alive because it gives us food and it's full of millions of networks that like coexist and talk to each other in order to take care of me.
sentences.zh: 世界确实是一个巨大的、有呼吸的有机体，它是活的，因为它给我们提供食物，它充满了数百万个共存并相互交流的网络，以便照顾我。

sentences.en: And it is sort of my great mother because it lets, you know, like that, that stuff isn't objective, but it is still something that like is true, right?
sentences.zh: 它某种程度上是我们的伟大母亲，因为它允许，你知道的，就像那样，那些东西虽然不客观，但它依然是某种真实存在的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, from a certain perspective, that objective and subjective mind don't know how to be in the same head.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从某种角度来看，那个客观心灵和主观心灵不知道该如何共存于同一个脑袋里。

sentences.en: And that the purpose of what, you know, Edward and Jersey Jungian, what he would see therapy doing is making them make sense,
sentences.zh: 而爱德华·埃丁格和荣格学派所认为的治疗的目的，就是让它们变得合理，

sentences.en: making them talk to each other and be on the same page so that even though they're opposites that don't understand each other and don't value each other's perspective,
sentences.zh: 让它们相互对话并达成共识，这样尽管它们是互不理解、也不认可对方视角的对立面，

sentences.en: there can be a harmony of that.
sentences.zh: 但它们之间可以有一种和谐。

sentences.en: There can be like a greater resonance in that paradox, whereas with a lot of people, most people,
sentences.zh: 在这个悖论中可以有一种更大的共鸣，然而对于很多人、大多数人来说，

sentences.en: they repress one and over identify with the other and then they resort to that other one in crisis.
sentences.zh: 他们压抑其中一个，过度认同另一个，然后在危机时又求助于那个被压抑的另一个。

sentences.en: I mean, think of all the like logical engineer types, like the people who like fight with you online and are like, oh, well, you had a feeling there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想所有那些逻辑工程师类型的家伙，比如那些在网上跟你争论，然后说：哦，你刚才产生了一种情绪。

sentences.en: Uh, that's a ad hominem, uh, absurdum, uh, mistake in logic.
sentences.zh: 呃，这是一个诉诸人身、呃，诉诸荒谬的逻辑错误。

sentences.en: I am just a perfectly logical being, sir.
sentences.zh: 先生，我只是一个完全理性的存在。

sentences.en: Like that person is emotionally nuts.
sentences.zh: 就像那种人在情感上简直是个疯子。

sentences.en: Like that person who's pretending to just be a calculator when they go into crisis, like you've all known these people, they become extremely over emotional and then break down.
sentences.zh: 就像那种在陷入危机时假装自己只是个计算器的人，你们都认识这样的人，他们变得极其情绪化然后崩溃。

sentences.en: And then a lot of times blame somebody else for that or deny that it happened.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候把这归咎于别人或者否认它发生过。

sentences.en: Same thing on the other side.
sentences.zh: 另一边也是如此。

sentences.en: What are people who live in a mystical space that is very, um, just open-ended and subjective and totally about my experience that I feel at any moment when they're in crisis?
sentences.zh: 那些生活在神秘空间里的人是什么样的？那个空间非常、嗯，开放且主观，完全关乎我在任何特定时刻所感受到的体验，当他们陷入危机时？

sentences.en: A lot of times those people become extremely logical and Edward, Edward Edinger in a way that is not fair or good, you know, um, like they cling to reason, um,
sentences.zh: 很多时候，那些人会变得极端理性，爱德华·埃丁格用一种并不公平也不好的方式，你知道的，嗯，比如他们紧紧抓住理性不放，

sentences.en: as a way of making meaning.
sentences.zh: 作为一种创造意义的方式。

sentences.zh: 当他们首选的创造意义的方式失效时，因为他们没有人类所需的那两种创造意义的方式，即主观和客观，

sentences.en: the ego and the unconscious self is Edinger's perspective.

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，爱德华·埃丁格这样做，嗯，我想算是一个不错的结局。

sentences.en: Um, I don't, I don't really have, I don't have a lot more and I, I need to hop off here, uh, and go get, get my kids.

sentences.en: But the, the thing that is relevant there, I think when you're looking at, you know, animism, ritual, whatever is we're never going to come up with the best way to, uh,

sentences.en: And we've been trying to grapple with that forever through anthropology, through, you know, uh, evolutionary biology, through psychology, through anthropology, through philosophy.
